description:
In the course of fixing clickhouse-local stress-test failures
(PR fix/clickhouse-local-stress, commits 4b6598786 / 6e344bdec /
451d228fc) we landed two correct-but-papering-over workarounds in the
platform layer:

1. `benchbox/platforms/clickhouse/workload.py` -- the DDL pipeline asks
   each benchmark for `dialect="duckdb"` and rewrites known DuckDB-only
   syntax in `_optimize_table_definition` (`Nullable() NOT NULL` strip,
   `FLOAT[N]` -> `Array(Float32)`, `DOUBLE[N]` -> `Array(Float64)`,
   ENGINE/ORDER BY injection). The cleaner shape would be for each
   benchmark schema to honour a real `dialect="clickhouse"` and emit
   ClickHouse-native DDL directly. We didn't do that because
   `transaction_primitives` and `write_primitives` drop their inline
   PRIMARY KEY when `dialect="clickhouse"` (per their pk_capability
   rule) and that PK string is what `_extract_primary_key_columns`
   reads to derive ORDER BY -- a global dialect swap would silently
   regress those tables to `ORDER BY tuple()`.

2. `benchbox/platforms/clickhouse/client.py` -- `ClickHouseLocalClient.execute()`
   uses `format="ArrowStream"` + pyarrow IPC decode instead of chDB's
   built-in `format="DataFrame"`, because the latter SIGABRTs
   (uncatchable) when the result contains a Tuple-typed column (e.g.
   `read_primitives.array_of_struct` returns `Array(Tuple(...))`). The
   SIGABRT also corrupts the on-disk `.chdb` directory (`recursive_mutex
   lock failed`), so subsequent benchmarks fail at session init with
   Code 722 / Code 36 BAD_ARGUMENTS. A `TODO(chdb-tuple-dataframe)`
   marker is in `_arrow_to_dataframe`.

Both workarounds are correct, but the underlying issues need upstream
fixes. Without explicit tracking, these workarounds will silently
linger after the upstream issues are resolved -- continuing to pay the
perf/clarity cost long after we could have reverted.

This TODO exists to:
- File the chdb DataFrame/Tuple SIGABRT upstream and link the issue
  from the `TODO(chdb-tuple-dataframe)` comment.
- Decide on a long-term plan for the DuckDB-as-ClickHouse-DDL hack
  (either fix the PK extraction to read schema metadata directly, or
  audit each schema for a real `dialect="clickhouse"` path).
- Keep a single index of every "papered over" platform workaround so
  future maintainers can sweep them when upstream catches up.

anti_patterns.dont: revert the workarounds until the upstream issues are confirmed fixed in a chdb release that BenchBox actually pins
anti_patterns.why: then BenchBox CI will start crashing again

anti_patterns.dont: silently rip out the FLOAT[N] regex rewrites before w2 reaches a decision

preserves.behavior: All benchmarks that currently land their inline PRIMARY KEY in the emitted DDL string (transaction_primitives, write_primitives) keep producing the same ORDER BY clause
ClickHouseLocalClient.execute() continues to handle SELECT, DDL, INSERT-no-params, and empty results correctly
Stress test (./scripts/local_stress_test.sh --scale 1 --platform clickhouse-local) still passes after any workaround replacement

work_units.notes:
Repro: `groupArray(tuple(Int32, Int32, Decimal, Decimal))` query
via `chdb.session.Session(...).query(sql, "DataFrame")` aborts
with SIGABRT (exit code 134, no stderr). `format="ArrowStream"`
returns clean Arrow IPC bytes for the same query. File at
https://github.com/chdb-io/chdb/issues with a minimal repro and
the chdb version (`uv pip show chdb` -- currently the bundled
version pinned by BenchBox). Update the
`TODO(chdb-tuple-dataframe)` comment in
`benchbox/platforms/clickhouse/client.py:_arrow_to_dataframe`
with the issue URL.
work_units.summary: File chdb DataFrame/Tuple SIGABRT upstream and link the issue

work_units.notes:
Two options to evaluate:
a) Teach `_extract_primary_key_columns` to read PKs from the
   benchmark schema dict (`benchmark.get_schema()`) rather than
   re-parsing the emitted DDL string. Then we can safely flip the
   workload to `dialect="clickhouse"` globally and drop the
   FLOAT[N]/DOUBLE[N] regex rewrites.
b) Audit every benchmark schema for a real `dialect="clickhouse"`
   path; ones that don't have one fall back to `"duckdb"` per the
   current behavior.
Document the chosen path in an ADR (or comment in workload.py)
and file follow-up TODOs for the implementation.

Create `docs/development/platform-workarounds.md` (or similar)
that lists every known "we worked around an upstream bug" hack:
  | File | Function | Upstream issue | Revert when |
  |------|----------|----------------|-------------|
  | clickhouse/client.py | _arrow_to_dataframe | chdb-io/chdb#NNN | Tuple SIGABRT fixed |
  | clickhouse/workload.py | _optimize_table_definition | (architectural) | PK extraction reworked |
Add a CONTRIBUTING.md note: "When you paper over an upstream bug,
add an entry here so we know when to revert."
work_units.summary: Add a single registry of platform workarounds for future cleanup sweeps
